Maya: Quick thread  We're designing how background jobs should authenticate to downstream services. Two options: hand the worker the org-scoped API key (ambient) or mint a delegated, short-lived token per job. Thoughts?
Liam: strongly prefer delegated tokens. Ambient keys are effectively permanent blast radius.
Sara: +1 but operational cost to mint on every job could be high. Can we amortize by minting per-job-type and caching for N minutes?
Maya: idea: mint tokens with claims {sub: worker, org: org-42, job: job-uuid, scopes: [...], billing_org: org-42} and ttl = clip(job_timeout + 2m, 30s, 1h). include jti for revocation.
Liam: good. include a "binding" claim for job_id so reuse across jobs is invalid. downstream services must check the job header matches claim.
Sara: agree on job_id binding, but how do we handle retries that exceed TTL? background dispatcher should, when retrying, either refresh token or request a token with a longer TTL when initiating a job. we need a refresh endpoint pattern.
Maya: proposal: token mint API supports an optional "expected_duration" param. broker can issue TTL = min(expected_duration + grace, max_ttl). if jobs extend beyond expected_duration, consumer calls /v1/token/refresh with jti and proof.
Liam: caching and RBAC: broker should resolve roles->scopes at mint time using the rolegraph. resolved scopes become authoritative in token. downstream services continue to perform policy checks against the token scopes. this avoids weird RBAC drift during execution.
Sara: caveat: when an admin revokes a role mid-run, tokens already minted might still be valid. we should define revocation semantics. immediate revoke via revocation list (check jti) for high-risk scopes; otherwise let tokens expire. revocation list lookups should be cheap (LRU + short TTL).
Maya: exactly. plan: maintain a revocation redis set keyed by jti; downstream caches consult it with a cheap bloom-filter-ish local cache updated every few seconds.
ops-bot: Notice: auth-broker-prod alert 2026-03-25T09:12:00Z - increased 503s from bkr-2.
Liam: fallback strategy if broker is unavailable: use a pre-provisioned service-account token with least privilege (narrowed scopes) that is rotated frequently by ops. never fall back to org ambient API key. emit metrics and page.
Sara: billing integration: some third-party connectors expect the "org api key" for chargeback. include a billing_org claim and a signed "billing_attestation" blob in token that billing can verify (or provide a mapping service that translates delegated token -> billing identity). tag @billing for product decision.
Maya: API sketch:
```
POST /v1/token/mint
Headers: Authorization: Bearer $BROKER_SVC_KEY
Body: {"actor":"worker:consumer","org":"org-42","requested_scopes":["read:data"],"expected_duration":120} 
Response: {"token":"ey...","expires_at":1755002580,"jti":"jti-123"}
```
and refresh:
```
POST /v1/token/refresh
Body: {"jti":"jti-123","proof":"<job-sig>"}
```
Design note: tokens are JWTs signed by broker key; downstream validates signature and claims.
Liam: logging/audit: mint event must record requester identity, resolved scopes, billing_org, job_id, jti, and decision path (rolegraph snapshot id). provide admin API to revoke by jti or job_id.
Sara: telemetry: emit mint latency, mint failures, cache hit/miss on rolegraph, and revocation check failures. also track fallback usage rate.
Maya: security check: ensure brokers require mTLS or service key auth. throttle mint calls from noisy queues.
Liam: ops runbook stub: if broker 5xx spike, automatically switch dispatchers to queue-level fallback tokens, page on-call, and enable a read-only mode for non-essential jobs.
Sara: UX note: expose a short CLI for devs to simulate minting and revoking tokens for local testing.
Maya: I'll pull this into a mini-RFC with claim schema, TTL heuristics, revocation model, fallback behavior, billing_attestation proposal, and runbook. will ping @product and @billing.
Liam: I can add details on rolegraph snapshotting and cache invalidation.
Sara: I'll write revocation TTL guidance and refresh flow.
Maya: cool thanks, posting RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
